headline: Harmony CPC signs letter of intent for Vimy Pharma takeover
dek: The non-binding agreement would take the private drug developer public on the TSX Venture Exchange as Vimy Pharmaceuticals Corp., with Beacon Securities leading a concurrent financing whose terms have not been disclosed.
caption: Harmony's shares are halted pending completion of the proposed qualifying transaction under TSXV Policy 2.4.

sources.title: Harmony Acquisitions Announces Proposed Qualifying Transaction with Vimy Pharmaceuticals

unverified_claims: The description of Vimy Pharma's management team, including the reference to former Novo Nordisk A/S executives, is provided by the companies. The release states this information has not been independently verified by Harmony's management.
The letter of intent is non-binding; there is no assurance the transaction proceeds on these or any terms.
Consideration, exchange ratio and the size and pricing of the concurrent financing have not been disclosed.
body: Harmony Acquisitions Corp. (TSXV: MONY.P), a capital pool company incorporated in British Columbia in May 2021, entered a non-binding letter of intent dated August 4 with Vimy Pharmaceuticals Inc. The parties intend a reverse takeover of Harmony that would constitute its qualifying transaction under TSXV Policy 2.4. Harmony's shares are halted pending completion.

Consideration and the exchange ratio were not disclosed. Beacon Securities Inc. is acting as lead agent and sole bookrunner on a concurrent financing whose size and pricing the companies say will follow in a comprehensive release. Closing requires TSXV acceptance and, if applicable, majority-of-the-minority shareholder approval. The resulting issuer would be named Vimy Pharmaceuticals Corp.

For the venture board, the read is on which sectors are still clearing the CPC route. A pharmaceutical developer taking the qualifying-transaction path rather than a conventional prospectus suggests the shell market remains the faster listing mechanism for pre-revenue life sciences. The absence of disclosed terms at announcement is ordinary at the letter-of-intent stage, not a signal either way.
